questions.q: Which Azure CLI command creates a new VNet along with its first subnet in a single call?
options: az network vnet create, using --subnet-name and --subnet-prefix alongside --address-prefix
az network subnet create, which creates the VNet automatically if it doesn't exist
az group create, which provisions a VNet by default in every resource group
There is no single command — the VNet and its subnet must always be created separately
questions.explain: az network vnet create requires at least one subnet to be specified at creation time via --subnet-name and --subnet-prefix, because a VNet can't exist with zero subnets.

questions.q: How many IP addresses does Azure reserve for its own use in every subnet, regardless of the subnet's size?
options: 5 — the network address, the default gateway, two for Azure DNS, and the broadcast address
0 — Azure only reserves addresses in subnets larger than a /24
10 — five at the start of the range and five at the end
1 — only the default gateway address is reserved
questions.explain: Every Azure subnet loses exactly 5 addresses to Azure's own use: the network address, the default gateway, two reserved for Azure DNS, and the broadcast address.

questions.q: A subnet is sized as a /28 (16 total addresses). How many addresses are actually usable for resources after Azure's reservations?
options: 0 — a /28 is too small to be a valid Azure subnet
questions.explain: 16 total addresses minus the 5 Azure always reserves leaves 11 usable addresses in a /28 subnet.

questions.q: Can a single Azure VNet span two regions, such as eastus and westeurope?
options: No — a VNet is a regional resource and exists in exactly one region
Yes, as long as both regions are in the same geography
Yes, but only if the VNet uses a /16 address space or larger
Yes, automatically, once a subnet in each region is created
questions.explain: A VNet lives in exactly one Azure region. Multi-region designs require separate VNets, one per region, connected afterward (e.g. via peering).

questions.q: What happens if you try to create a new subnet whose address range overlaps an existing subnet in the same VNet?
options: Azure rejects the create call — subnet ranges within a VNet must be unique and non-overlapping
Azure automatically shrinks the new subnet to avoid the overlap
Azure merges the two subnets into one
It succeeds, but only one of the two subnets will route traffic
questions.explain: Every subnet's address range must be unique and non-overlapping within its VNet; Azure rejects the creation if the ranges collide.
